title: Finite-presentation approximation on a space affine over a Noetherian space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $f$ is affine: for every affine scheme $V\to Y$, the fibre sheaf $X\times_Y V$ is represented by an affine scheme. Assume $Y$ is Noetherian: its underlying point space is quasi-compact, its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests, and it admits a surjective etale map from a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] (some etale scheme atlas is locally Noetherian). The point topology is [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Work with module sheaves on the small etale ringed sites and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module is finitely presented if etale locally it has an exact sequence $\mathcal O_X^m\to\mathcal O_X^n\to\mathcal F\to0$ with finite $m,n$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$, there exist a small filtered category $J$, a diagram of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F_j$, and compatible maps $\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal M$ which exhibit $\mathcal M$ as their colimit in all $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No finite-type hypothesis on $f$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Since $|Y|$ is quasi-compact, [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] gives an affine scheme $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with a representable surjective etale map $V\to Y$. As $V$ is quasi-compact, $Y$ is quasi-compact in the chart sense of [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests by hypothesis. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since $f$ is affine. Moreover $|X|$ is quasi-compact, as step 6 needs: $U=X\times_YV$ is an affine scheme by the affineness hypothesis, $U\to X$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so $|U|\to|X|$ is surjective, and it is continuous by the definition of the topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; the image of the quasi-compact space $|U|$ is $|X|$. Use the small site models fixed by the size convention. The category of module sheaves is abelian and has small colimits by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. For any quasi-coherent module $T$ on $X$, [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] says that $f_*T$ is quasi-coherent. No finite-type assumption on $f$ or Noetherian assumption on $X$ has entered.

The Noetherian hypothesis of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-filtered-union] holds for $Y$: quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are checked in step 1. Let $W\to Y$ be any etale scheme chart and $V'\to Y$ the given surjective etale map from a locally Noetherian scheme. Then $W'=W\times_YV'$ is a scheme, etale over $V'$ and surjective etale over $W$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. As $W'\to V'$ is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], $W'$ is covered by affine opens of finite type over Noetherian affine opens of $V'$, which are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. So $W'$, hence $W$ [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent], is locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-filtered-union] to $f_*T$. Let $I_T$ be its nonempty directed set of coherent submodules $H_i$; their canonical colimit in all module sheaves is $f_*T$. Each $H_i$ is finitely presented. Indeed its restriction to an etale scheme chart is the etale realization of a coherent Zariski module, by the meaning of coherent in the cited statement. On that scheme [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation] gives a finite free presentation locally. The forward equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] is tensor pullback, hence a left adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]; it carries this cokernel presentation to the same finite free presentation on the etale site. Finite presentation on a covering chart suffices by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus].

Put $P_i=f^*H_i$. Pullback is the tensor-formula left adjoint of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Consequently it preserves colimits and finite free modules, so $P:=\varinjlim_i P_i\simeq f^*f_*T$. To check finite presentation of $P_i$, pull a local finite free presentation of $H_i$ back along $f$: the inverse image of its covering is a covering, and right exactness gives $\mathcal O_X^m\to\mathcal O_X^n\to P_i\to0$ there. The etale-local identifications with restriction and the compatibility of the two paths of pullback are given by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Also $P_i$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent].

The counit $e_T:P\simeq f^*f_*T\to T$ is surjective. Choose an affine surjective etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. By affineness, $U=X\times_YV=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, and $U\to X$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The comparisons of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identify the restricted counit with the counit for $U\to V$. For $N=T(U)$, affine chart calculus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] identifies this with the sheaf associated to $B\otimes_A N\to N$. The tensor adjunction realization [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] identifies the arrow itself with $b\otimes n\mapsto bn$. It is onto since $n$ is the image of $1\otimes n$. Surjectivity of a sheaf map is local on a cover, so $e_T$ is onto on $X$. Thus steps 1--4 give, for every quasi-coherent $T$, a surjection from a small directed colimit of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules.

Apply this construction to $T=\mathcal M$, writing $P=\varinjlim_{i\in I}P_i$ and $e:P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], $P$ and $N=\ker(e)$ are quasi-coherent. Apply the very same construction of steps 1--4 to $T=N$: it gives $Q=\varinjlim_{j\in J}Q_j\twoheadrightarrow N$, with $J$ small nonempty directed and each $Q_j$ finitely presented and quasi-coherent. Let $d:Q\to N\hookrightarrow P$. Its image is exactly $N$, hence $\mathcal M$ is the cokernel of $d$ in the abelian module category.

Write $p_i:P_i\to P$, $q_j:Q_j\to Q$, and denote the transition maps by $P_{ii'}$ and $Q_{jj'}$. Let $K$ be the set of triples $(i,j,a)$ with $a:Q_j\to P_i$ and $p_i a=dq_j$. Order these by $(i,j,a)\le(i',j',a')$ when $i\le i'$, $j\le j'$, and $P_{ii'}a=a'Q_{jj'}$. This is a partially ordered set. All its hom sets and indices lie in the chosen bound, so it is small. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-hom-colimit], every $dq_j$ factors through some $P_i$: $|X|$ is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated by step 1, and $Q_j$ is finitely presented. Thus $K$ is nonempty, and for each $j$ there is a triple having that second index.

To give a common upper bound for $(i,j,a)$ and $(i',j',a')$, choose $j_0\ge j,j'$. Factor $dq_{j_0}$ through some $P_h$ using [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-hom-colimit], then enlarge $h$ to dominate $i,i'$. The two maps from $Q_j$ to $P_h$, one obtained from $a$, the other from $Q_j\to Q_{j_0}\to P_h$, become equal in $P$. The eventual-equality assertion of the same cited node gives a later index where they agree. Do the same for $Q_{j'}$ and pass to a common later index $h_1$. The resulting factorization $Q_{j_0}\to P_{h_1}$ defines a triple above both given triples. Hence $K$ is directed. Notice that eventual equality is needed here; factorization alone would not prove directedness.

For $k=(i,j,a)$ put $C_k=\operatorname{coker}(a)$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. It is finitely presented by the following local presentation argument. Locally choose $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^n\to P_i\to0$ and finitely many generators of $Q_j$. After a further covering, lift the images of these finitely many generators to $\mathcal O^n$. Adding these finitely many lifts to the $r$ existing relations presents $C_k$ as a cokernel $\mathcal O^{r+m}\to\mathcal O^n\to C_k\to0$. This argument works on any ringed site and uses no Noetherianity. Every ordered pair of triples gives a commuting square of arrows $a$, hence a canonical map of cokernels. These compose uniquely by the cokernel universal property. Since $ed=0$, each $C_k$ has a compatible map to $\mathcal M$.

The two projection diagrams over $K$ still have colimits $P$ and $Q$. For the first projection, every $i\in I$ is below the first index of some triple: start with any triple and enlarge its first index to dominate $i$, composing its arrow with the transition. For the second projection, every $j\in J$ occurs by step 6. Directedness then makes the triples above any fixed index nonempty and directed. Explicitly, a compatible family of maps $P_{i(k)}\to L$ therefore extends uniquely to all $P_i$: choose a triple with first index at least $i$ and restrict its map; a common upper bound proves independence of the choice and compatibility. The identical argument applies to $Q_j$. Now compatible maps $C_k\to L$ are precisely compatible maps $P_{i(k)}\to L$ killing each $a_k$. By these projection identifications they are precisely maps $P\to L$ killing $d$, since the maps $Q_{j(k)}\to Q$ are jointly colimiting. They are therefore precisely maps $\mathcal M=\operatorname{coker}(d)\to L$. This is the colimit universal property in all module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus $\mathcal M\simeq\varinjlim_{k\in K}C_k$, with the compatible maps of step 8. The small directed poset $K$, regarded as a category, is the required small filtered category.
